A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAG research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I. Inspection of all 13 pages in each version supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations, baseline comparisons, ablations, defense tests, and transferability results in Section 6, plus timing results and real-world examples in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendices F–G; retained results still qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same text-conditioned U-Net trigger generator, joint training, reconstruction and language-model losses, data preparation, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and COCO-2017, with the same additional photographs, webpage, and GUI examples in Appendix G. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains BadEncoder and TrojVLM as attack comparators; Table 3 retains Spectral Signature, Beatrix, and PAR as defenses. The same three victim VLMs are evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices C–D retain the same splits, preprocessing, IoU-based metrics, default 5% poisoning rate, 100-target restricted comparison, and training and inference settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, defense evaluations, cross-dataset transfer tests, poison-rate sensitivity, timing analysis, and qualitative case studies are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Both report timing means and standard deviations over 10 sampled questions in Section 6.2 and Appendix F. Neither adds seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 retains InternVL-2.5-8B ASR@0.5 of 66.7% on RefCOCO testA and 71.2% on RefCOCO+ testA. No result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, existence and convergence propositions, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs—including the four convergence lemmas—are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, feasibility, effectiveness, stealthiness, and transferability claims. The added citations do not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 6–7 retain the same interpretations of defense resistance, transferability, lower success rates in open-vocabulary generation, and vulnerability through visual inputs. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The hardware, pseudocode, data processing, hyperparameters, and defense descriptions remain unchanged. Appendix I still promises release of code and datasets upon acceptance, without new access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds four introductory citations and bibliography entries: MC-LLaVA, UniC-Tokens, QCRD, and Advancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multi-Scale Alignment in Multi-Modal Models. This is a limited background expansion; the discussion distinguishing IAG from prior attacks is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to the added inline citations, corresponding citation-suffix adjustments, and updated arXiv version/date stamp. Explanatory prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation additions cause limited column reflow in the introduction and bibliography on pages 1 and 8–9. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–8 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds four background references and makes minor presentation adjustments, while retaining the same scientific arguments, empirical evidence, proofs, interpretations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. These limited bibliographic edits leave overall paper quality materially unchanged.
